protocol.target: attention-only MLP output minus plain generated-cproj MLP output on identical held-out tokens
protocol.caveat: Separately co-adapted terminal checkpoints define an endpoint proxy rather than an isolated causal optimum.

conclusions: Activation weighting makes the paired fixed-basis span more relevant than its raw-weight chance alignment, but its best possible diagonal still explains only 0.326 percent of the matched output correction.
Removing same-index pairing while keeping both bases fixed raises optimal functional coverage to 4.324 percent, a 13.27-fold increase. Pairing is therefore a major expressivity bottleneck.

Both trained diagonals point away from the endpoint proxy and use only 8 to 12 percent of the optimal paired correction output norm. The observed CE failure is consistent with both insufficient paired capacity and poor task-driven use of that capacity.

A zero-initialized learned 64x64 core between the same frozen bases is the narrowest evidence-backed next screen. It adds cross-basis mixing without learning input/output bases; it must still be described honestly as a fixed-subspace low-rank residual.

next_screen.mechanism: fixed FHT-derived input/output bases with a zero-initialized Muon-owned 64x64 core and unit outer scale
next_screen.promotion_rule: 0.5TPP only; require a material fixed-eval gain over plain, grouped, and both diagonal controls before any 5TPP promotion
